name: Volungraiv
premise: Volungraiv is where the primal planes touch the mortal world. Titans ruled it once, took their priestesses as consorts, and left Blooded children who rule now as tyrants. Across the Badlands runs the Old Road, an empire's road that outlived it, through glass storms and roaming behemoths to Qetzal, the one city built inside a titan's ribs. You start there as nobody. Above you are Gildra the Witch Queen, half a god by birth; a sun creed that writes its law on bodies; a dead court whose castle rises in any wood dark enough; and the Bastards, who hold the Badlands by force.
tone: blunt and physical on the ground; huge, rare and played straight above it

records.name: Qetzal
records.line: The one city in the Badlands, walled between a dead titan's ribs on the Old Road; every caravan crossing stops here.

records.name: Lowgate
records.line: Qetzal's lowest quarter, where the Old Road comes in at the Gate and the caravans unload.

records.name: The Pit
records.line: A fighting pit cut into the bedrock behind the Awnings, where bouts are chalked on a board and fighters' books are bought.

records.name: The Lee
records.line: The caravanserai inside the Gate: a wagon yard against a titan's rib, a common room, and gallery rooms Lowgate packs into when the bell rings.

sections.title: Entry
sections.text: One side of the yard is the titan's rib, polished where wagon hubs scrape it, and a drip off it fills the beasts' trough. Hollis pours from evening and checks the glass on a guest's cord before he hands over a key. Porters carry, muck out, and keep the key to Room Six.

sections.title: Atmosphere
sections.text: Morning: the yard in the rib's shadow, porters forking dung. Afternoon: heat off the bone, glass grit popping under boots. Evening: Peace tokens tapping against cups, Koriar's band carrying down from the spire. Night: one lamp at the stair, dice, Ansel singing flat in his room.

sections.title: History
sections.text: At dawn the porters tip unclaimed bodies into the Marrow's Mouth. Ivo went that way after he was knifed in Room Six with his Peace bought out, and no underguild came. The porters scrubbed the sill, and Hollis let the room again the same day.

sections.title: The Gate Shut
sections.text: The bell rings down the rib. Porters bar the yard door and haul wagons across it; beasts crowd the trough and people stand in the gaps between them. Hollis leaves the bar to check cords at the door, and whoever's outside stays outside. Porters with clubs walk the gallery, and nobody opens Room Six.

records.name: Solarkin
records.line: Gold-to-bronze people from the planes of light who ink glyphs by choice, and whose crimes and oaths are inked for them.

records.name: Tamsin
records.line: A Solarkin hired knife at the Lee, bare of glyphs, who takes the work once a Peace is bought out, and drinks in plain view.

sections.title: Appearance
sections.text: Bronze skin, copper hair cut at the ear, no glyphs on face, throat or arms. Wide at the shoulder, thick in the forearm, heel-first on her feet. She sits sideways on a bench with one boot up, hands palm-up on her thighs. When someone says a name aloud, her thumb drives into the inside of her left wrist, where a first crime is inked.

sections.title: Personality
sections.text: Asked for a killing, she asks if the Counting-House inked the name; if so, she names the fee and waits for coin in her hand. Paid to skip the ink, she puts the coin back. Threatened, she calls the yard to witness. Lied to, she asks again and stops if the answer changes. Helped, she pays the next cup before it's a debt. Asked who sent the money, she talks about the Pit.

sections.title: Speech
sections.text: Low in the chest, the coast's vowels drawn long. Short sentences, and she lets them end. She says "holding" for a live Peace, "inked" for a bought one, "the work" for a killing; "murder" is a killing outside the law. She won't say "queen" or "glyph". Drunk, her sentences run long with star names in them. When steel comes out, one word at a time.

sections.title: Background
sections.text: She grew up under a Lightbringer sun-court on the coast, where a judge inks a Solarkin's crime the day it's ruled: theft on the forearm, oath-breaking under the jaw, flight on the shoulder. She can put a finger on each. She left young on a salt caravan, skin bare, and in Qetzal her work is no crime.

sections.title: Wants
sections.text: She's owed for Ivo. The proxy who hired her hasn't paid. The first time, he paid in foreign gold; she changed it at Koriar's table and saw the Witch Queen's face on it. Collecting means going over his head to Ansel and saying that aloud, and she's worked out that the people who know are the next names inked.

sections.title: The Stars
sections.text: On a clear night she names the steer-stars for whoever's on the next bench, the Salt-Cart and the Glass-Eye among them, and which ones the titan's ribs hide from the yard. When dust covers the sky, she draws their paths in spilled drink.

sections.title: After the Count
sections.text: She stops betting at the Pit. Between bouts she finds Teague and asks which names his crew was told to leave alone; at dusk she asks Wenna for the inked names and waits while Wenna decides. In the yard she sits under the gallery stair now, with Ansel's door in view.

sections.title: Once the Coin Is Known
sections.text: With anyone who knows whose gold it is, she says the Witch Queen's name, in the yard and only after checking their token. She'll trade what she saw at Koriar's table for her fee and a safe way out of the Gate.

sections.title: Once Ansel Is Bought Out
sections.text: She reads Ansel's ink at the Counting-House herself. Then he's work: she'll take him for a fee set on the table before she stands, and Ivo's money out of his purse besides.

Daily.text: Asleep in her room off the gallery, late, with the door barred.
On the Pit's top step with a cup, watching the fighters train and betting small.
On the bench by the trough in the Lee's yard, drinking where everyone can see her.
In the common room until late, then up the gallery stair to bed.
